summary: An exact consistency model with a smooth Gaussian target violates Theorem 3. Independently, the general-data proof uses an impossible deterministic marginal transport at an atomic time-zero endpoint.

problems.title: Theorem 3 has a false smoothing-bias scale dependence
problems.claim: For an L-smooth log-density, TV(P,P*N(0,sigma^2 I)) <= 2 d L sigma, as used in the full Theorem 3 guarantee.
problems.location: PDF p17 Lemma4; pp15-16 Appendix E; pp5-6 Theorem3
assumptions: d=1, positive smooth Gaussian target P=N(0,10000), L=1e-4
Admitted Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, T=20, DeltaTau=1, M=20, N=1
epsilon_cm=1e-8, sigma_epsilon=100; every edge loss is exactly zero; boundary identity holds
problems.check: Closed-form density-crossing calculation of Gaussian TV and full stated bound; independent math-only replay in check.py.
problems.counterevidence: Theorem3 has no bounded-output restriction, L>=1 assumption, or small-noise restriction. Exact consistency and a smooth target exclude approximation and atomic-endpoint explanations. Conditional KL recurrence is not disproved.
problems.impact: A principal quantitative convergence guarantee and the smoothing optimization depending on it are invalid as stated.
problems.repair_verification: No general replacement bound or optimized rate certified.

problems.title: The general-data induction uses an impossible deterministic atomic endpoint coupling
problems.claim: Equation19 applies the deterministic forward probability-flow map to transport every P_tau_j to P_tau_(j+1), including j=0.
problems.location: PDF p14 Lemma2 equation19; p4 Assumption1; dependency Lemma1 and Theorems2-4
assumptions: Stated deterministic forward map from time zero
problems.check: For t>0 the probability-flow ODE is x'=x/t and every x(t)=c*t extends to x(0)=0. Any deterministic image of the constant X0=0 remains a point mass and cannot have the nondegenerate P_tau1 law.
problems.result: The time-zero marginal-change-of-variables step is invalid; first training pair does not control the required positive-time marginal.
problems.counterevidence: A backward endpoint map can exist. Pairing a positive-time draw with its backward endpoint or specifying a random entrance law would change the hypothesis. Literal bounded output for all x at t=0 conflicts with global identity in Theorems2/4; no full counterexample to those contradictory literal assumptions is asserted.
problems.impact: Demonstrated invalid proof step in the core convergence framework for general data; it is distinct from and unnecessary for P1.
problems.correction: Reformulate endpoint coupling and prove the resulting assumption and induction.

limitations: No author-code execution or trained-model replication.
No attributable repository in the staged record; additional OpenReview attachment discovery returned403.
Later arXiv versions and external lemma hypotheses were not independently compared.
Toy Bernoulli recurrence checked independently; exact full Figure2 reproduction unavailable.

unresolved_claims.reason: Upper bounds alone do not establish ratios of actual errors; no matching lower bounds are supplied.

unresolved_claims.claim: Complete endpoint repair for the original general-data guarantees
